ENEL 585 – Switch-Related Losses and Thermal Limits

Topic 14

Dr. Philippe Gray

Department of Electrical & Software Engineering

Switch-Related Losses: The Plan

Topic 13 showed the magnetics side of \(f_{sw}\): halving it from 500 to 250 kHz doubled \(L\), and the winding no longer fit. Real switches are the other side: their loss grows with \(f_{sw}\).

  1. Conduction loss: power lost while on — independent of \(f_{sw}\)
  2. Hard switching: \(V\)–\(I\) overlap at turn-on and turn-off — scales with \(f_{sw}\)
  3. Datasheet to junction temperature: a SiC MOSFET loss budget and heatsink stack
  4. Frequency trade-off & soft switching: pushing \(f_{sw}\) up without overheating the die

Conduction Loss: MOSFET vs. Diode and IGBT

MOSFET lines: Wolfspeed C3M0021120K (21 mΩ at 25 °C, 38 mΩ at 175 °C). Red line: a model, \(V_F=1.0\) V, \(r_d=10\) mΩ

Above \(I=V_F/(R_{DS(\text{on})}-r_d)=36\) A the hot MOSFET drops more than this model line: a constant-drop device wins at high current. For real parts, compare their datasheet curves.

Two on-state models (independent of \(f_{sw}\))

  1. Resistive (MOSFET channel): \(v_{\text{on}}=R_{DS(\text{on})}\,i\), so \[ P_{\text{cond}}=I_{\text{rms}}^2\,R_{DS(\text{on})} \] with \(I_{\text{rms}}\) taken of the device’s own current. \(R_{DS(\text{on})}\) rises \(1.8\times\) from 25 °C to 175 °C here: use the hot value.
  1. Constant drop + slope (Diode / IGBT): \(v_{\text{on}}=V_F+r_d\,i\), so \[ P_{\text{cond}}=V_F\,I_{\text{avg}}+r_d\,I_{\text{rms}}^2 \]
  1. Example (Topic 13 buck, 100 V → 50 V, \(I_o=10\) A, \(D=0.5\)): \(I_{Q,\text{rms}}=I_o\sqrt{D}=7.07\) A, \(I_{D,\text{avg}}=(1-D)I_o=5.0\) A. \(Q\) and \(D\) carry the same pulses: a 38 mΩ MOSFET in either place loses 1.9 W, a \(V_F=1.0\) V diode (\(r_d\) neglected) 5.0 W. The diode costs \((1-D)V_F/V_o=1\) % of the output here, but 22 % at 12 V → 3.3 V (\(D=0.28\)): low-voltage converters replace \(D\) with a MOSFET (synchronous rectification).

Hard Switching: Clamped Inductive Transition

Inside \(Q\) (dashed): in \(t_{ri}\), \(D\) still conducts and holds the switch node at 0, so \(v_{DS}=V_d\) and \(Q\)’s drain–source capacitance \(C_{oss}\) cannot discharge. In \(t_{fv}\) it discharges through the channel, which loses \(E_{\text{on}}+E_{oss}\) (\(E_{oss}\): \(C_{oss}\)’s energy at \(V_d\)). In \(t_{rv}\), \(I_L\) recharges \(C_{oss}\): the channel loses \(E_{\text{off}}-E_{oss}\). Same sum.

Why \(v_{DS}\) and \(i_Q\) must overlap

  1. Turn-on (gate on, delay omitted): before \(Q\) closes, \(D\) carries \(I_L\), clamping the switch node so \(v_{DS}=V_d\). \(v_{DS}\) cannot fall until \(i_Q\) reaches \(I_L\) and turns \(D\) off: \(t_{\text{on}}=t_{ri}+t_{fv}\), current rise then voltage fall.
  1. Turn-off: \(D\) stays reverse-biased until \(v_{DS}\) rises to \(V_d\). Only then can \(D\) take \(I_L\) so \(i_Q\) falls to zero: \(t_{\text{off}}=t_{rv}+t_{fi}\), voltage rise then current fall.
  1. Power triangles: high \(V_d\) and high \(I_L\) overlap twice per cycle: \[ E_{\text{on}}\approx\tfrac12 V_dI_Lt_{\text{on}},\qquad E_{\text{off}}\approx\tfrac12 V_dI_Lt_{\text{off}} \] \[ P_{\text{sw}}=(E_{\text{on}}+E_{\text{off}})\,f_{sw}\approx\tfrac12 V_dI_L(t_{\text{on}}+t_{\text{off}})\,f_{sw} \]

From Datasheet to Junction Temperature

Buck, 800 V → 400 V, 50 A (\(D=0.5\), 20 kW), \(f_{sw}=25\) kHz, with the Wolfspeed C3M0021120K (Topic 9, TO-247-4)

With no heatsink (\(R_{\theta JA}=40\ ^\circ\text{C/W}\)) the part sheds only 3.4 W at \(T_j=175\) °C, \(T_a=40\) °C.

For another operating point: \(P_{\text{cond}}=I_{\text{rms}}^2R_{DS(\text{on})}\) (hot); scale \(E_{\text{on}},E_{\text{off}}\) roughly \(\propto V_dI_L\) from the 800 V, 50 A test point (or read the datasheet’s \(E\) vs. \(I_D\) curves); \(P=P_{\text{cond}}+(E_{\text{on}}+E_{\text{off}})f_{sw}\); check \(T_j=T_a+R_{\theta,\text{tot}}P<T_{j,\max}\).

Worst-case loss budget (175 °C datasheet values)

  1. Conduction: \(R_{DS(\text{on})}=38\text{ m}\Omega\) (hot), \(I_{Q,\text{rms}}=50\sqrt{0.5}=35.4\text{ A}\Rightarrow P_{\text{cond}}=47.5\text{ W}\).
  2. Switching (tested with a SiC Schottky diode): \(E_{\text{on}}=0.69\text{ mJ}\), \(E_{\text{off}}=0.42\text{ mJ}\Rightarrow P_{\text{sw}}=1.11\text{ mJ}\times 25\text{ kHz}=27.8\text{ W}\).
  3. Total die loss: \(P=47.5+27.8=\mathbf{75.3\text{ W}}\) (gate drive, 0.08 W, is mostly outside the die).

Heatsink thermal stack (\(T_a=40\,^\circ\text{C}\))

Topic 13’s \(\Delta T=R_{th}P\), three in series (datasheets write \(R_\theta\)): \[ T_j=T_a+\bigl(R_{\theta JC}+R_{\theta CS}+R_{\theta SA}\bigr)\,P \] \(R_{\theta,\text{tot}}=0.32\) (datasheet) \(+\,0.40+0.80\) (assumed) \(=1.52\ ^\circ\text{C/W}\), so \(T_j=40+1.52\times 75.3=\mathbf{154\,^\circ\text{C}}<175\,^\circ\text{C}\) ✓.

The Frequency Trade-Off and Design Levers

Last slide’s example: C3M0021120K, 800 V, 50 A, \(D=0.5\), 175 °C values, \(R_{\theta,\text{tot}}=1.52\) °C/W, \(T_a=40\) °C

Putting Topic 13 and Topic 14 together

  1. Higher \(f_{sw}\) shrinks magnetics but grows \(P_{\text{sw}}\): the 89 W ceiling allows \(f_{\max}\approx37\) kHz; 50 kHz gives 103 W, \(T_j\ge197\,^\circ\text{C}>T_{j,\max}\).
  1. Raise the ceiling or cut loss per die: lower \(R_{\theta SA}\) raises \(P_{\max}\); two in parallel at \(I_L/2\) each have ¼ the conduction loss.
  1. Faster gate drive (smaller \(R_g\)) cuts \(P_{\text{sw}}\) but raises \(dv/dt\), \(di/dt\): overshoot, ringing, EMI, false turn-on of the leg’s other switch.
  1. Choose the device technology:
    • Si MOSFET: lowest \(R_{DS(\text{on})}\) at low voltage; slow diode
    • IGBT: low drop at high current; a turn-off tail limits hard switching to 10–30 kHz (stations: 5–10 kHz)
    • SiC, GaN: fast, little diode recovery (GaN ≤ 650 V)

ZVS in a Buck: Let the Inductor Current Reverse

Example: \(V_d=48\) V, \(V_o=12\) V, \(f_s=200\) kHz, \(L=7.5\,\mu\)H, \(I_o=2\) A, so \(\Delta i_L=6\) A and \(i_L\) runs from \(-1\) A to \(5\) A

Other converters get the reversed current from a resonant tank (LLC) or a transformer’s leakage inductance (dual active bridge).

How a buck gets zero-voltage turn-on

  1. Zero-voltage switching (ZVS), a soft-switching method: \(v_{DS}=0\) when the gate turns on, so no V–I overlap: no \(E_{\text{on}}\), no \(E_{oss}\) lost.
  2. Dead time: both switches are briefly off at each edge; only \(i_L\) moves \(v_{DS,L}\).
  1. Edge A, \(i_L=5\) A \(>0\): \(i_L\) leaves the node, so \(v_{DS,L}\) falls to 0 and \(Q_L\) turns on at zero voltage. Every buck does this.
  1. Edge B, \(i_L=-1\) A \(<0\): \(i_L\) enters the node, so \(v_{DS,L}\) rises to \(V_d\): \(Q_H\) also turns on at zero voltage, if \(\Delta i_L/2>I_o\).
  1. The cost: \(I_{L,\text{rms}}=2.65\) A, against 2 A with small ripple: 75 % more \(I^2R\) loss.

Inside Edge B: The Current Swings the Switch Node

Last slide’s buck: \(C_{oss}=500\) pF per switch (taken constant), \(t_d=80\) ns, \(V_o\) constant over the edge. \(v_{DS,H}=V_d-v_{DS,L}\); \(i_{QH}\) includes the current in \(Q_H\)’s \(C_{oss}\).

From \(Q_L\) off to \(Q_H\) on

  1. \(0\) to \(49\) ns, both off: \(i_L\) splits equally between the two \(C_{oss}\); \(v_{DS,H}\) falls at \(|i_L|/(2C_{oss})\approx 1\) V/ns. \(i_{QH}=i_L/2\) leaves \(Q_H\)’s drain for \(V_d\): \(p_{QH}<0\) returns \(E_{oss}=\tfrac12C_{oss}V_d^2=0.58\,\mu\)J.
  1. At \(49\) ns, \(v_{DS,H}=0\): both \(C_{oss}\) stop changing, so \(Q_H\)’s body diode takes all of \(i_L\) (\(i_{QH}\) steps).
  1. At \(t_d=80\) ns, \(Q_H\) gated on at \(v_{DS,H}=0\): no overlap, so \(E_{\text{on}}\approx 0\) and no \(E_{oss}\) lost.
  1. The limit: \(v_{DS,H}\) must reach 0 by \(t_d\), or \(Q_H\) turns on partly hard. Smaller \(|i_L|\) swings slower; the swing just fills \(t_d\) at \(i_L=I_o-\Delta i_L/2=-0.63\) A, so ZVS needs \(I_o\le 2.37\) A.
